DISCUSSION
The fundamental philosophy behind any closed loop feedback system is the same.
Regardless of how complicated a feedback system seems, a systematic troubleshooting approach will yield good results.
The systems should first be analyzed using a Macroscopic approach.
The problem can then be reduced to a microscopic level.
A macroscopic approach to a feedback system can be represented in a block diagram.
Notice that the output of the motor affects the input.
In the case of the 280 trainer, the feedback system is simple.
The macroscopic approach is to isolate the fault to the 280 Trainer or 130 Test Console cards.
The microscopic view might be one portion of the feedback path.
Once the problem is isolated to the microscopic level, you then troubleshoot down to the component like in any electronic circuit. Inductor Capacitor Resistor
Troubleshooting should initially be approached using a _______ point of view.

1. When troubleshooting, begin with a macroscopic approach and work your way down to a component level..
2. First, recognize the problem and make certain the problem is not human engineered.
3. Make sure that the problem is not in the motor itself. tput Controlling Input Circuitry Motor Input Output Closed Loop Feedback System
4. Isolate the controlling circuitry by verifying that there is an input signal and an output signal.
5. If there is a solid input and a good output, then the controlling circuitry is fine.
6. If the motor is running but no signal is being applied to the controlling circuitry, examine the sensing circuitry. 130-280 Controlling Interface Circuitry Output Input Sensing
7. If there is a good input to the controlling circuitry but no output, reduce the problem to the component level inside the controlling circuit. a Corp.
